results.question: Seed-VC: license (GPL-3.0?), zero-shot reference length (1-30s), the claimed real-time latency of about 300ms, and Mac support. Does efegen/rvc-pipeline exist, under what license, and does it need 6GB VRAM?
results.finding:
LICENSE: GPL-3.0 is confirmed for the code (LICENSE file is GNU GPL v3; GitHub API spdx GPL-3.0). The HF weights Plachta/Seed-VC are also tagged license: gpl-3.0 and are ungated.

The stack has not been maintained since 2025: Plachtaa/seed-vc was ARCHIVED (read-only) on 2025-11-21 (GraphQL archivedAt), with the last push on 2025-04-20. ASTRAL-quantization, the GPL-3.0 tokenizer used by the V2 model, was archived the same day. There will be no fixes for new PyTorch or macOS releases.

The singing (SVC) path also downloads third-party weights:
- rmvpe.pt from lj1995/VoiceConversionWebUI (MIT tag plus a research-only rider; see voice-1)
- funasr/campplus (Apache-2.0)
- nvidia/bigvgan_v2_44khz_128band_512x (MIT)
- openai/whisper-small (Apache-2.0)

REFERENCE LENGTH: the README says 'clone a voice given a reference speech of 1~30 seconds'. However, inference.py truncates the reference to 25 s (ref_audio[:sr * 25]), so the effective v1 cap is 25 s. The arXiv paper 2411.09943 (Songting Liu, 2024-11-15) gives no length bounds.

LATENCY: '300 ms' is only the algorithm delay. The README says 'algorithm delay of ~300ms and device side delay of ~100ms', so total is about 400 ms. Its own benchmark table (RTX 3060 Laptop GPU) shows 430 ms latency and 150 ms inference per chunk. That figure is for seed-uvit-xlsr-tiny, a 25M-parameter, 22.05 kHz speech VC model. It is not the 200M, 44.1 kHz singing model, which has no published real-time figures. The README strongly recommends a GPU for real time. A '300 ms live singing jam' is therefore an overstatement: vendor-claimed, speech-model only, and algorithm delay only.

MAC: officially supported since the 2025-03-03 changelog entry ('Added Mac M Series (Apple Silicon) support'). requirements-mac.txt exists, and inference.py, inference_v2.py, app_svc.py and real-time-gui.py select the mps device. Caveats:
- requirements-mac.txt installs an UNPINNED PyTorch nightly pre-release ('torch --pre ... whl/nightly/cpu').
- A known tkinter issue affects the real-time GUI on Mac.
- The repo is archived, so Mac breakage will not be fixed upstream.

GPL CONSEQUENCE: private personal use is unconstrained, and GPL does not cover generated audio. If AURA is distributed and imports Seed-VC modules in-process, the distributed combination must be GPL-3.0-compatible. Keeping it behind a separate-process/CLI boundary is the usual way to avoid that; that is a legal interpretation, not stated by the repo.

efegen/rvc-pipeline: DOES NOT EXIST publicly.
- The GitHub API returns 404 and github.com/efegen/rvc-pipeline returns 404.
- The user 'efegen' exists but has only 3 public repos, all unrelated (analysis-projects, okaliptus-studio, yapay-zeka-sinav-kocu).
- There are no HF spaces, models or datasets by efegen, PyPI 'rvc-pipeline' returns 404, and a web search found nothing.

Its license and the '6GB VRAM' requirement are therefore unverifiable. The repo is probably a hallucinated citation in the Kimi source. Similarly named repos exist (for example Ryouko-Yamanda65777/rvc-pipeline with no license, and Kisechan/rvc-conversion-pipeline), but none can be tied to the claim.
results.corrected_value: Seed-VC: GPL-3.0 for code AND HF weights (confirmed), but the repo has been ARCHIVED since 2025-11-21. Reference: 1-30 s per the README, but the code truncates it to 25 s. Real-time: about 300 ms algorithm delay plus about 100 ms device delay (about 400 ms total); 430 ms measured by the vendor on an RTX 3060 Laptop for the tiny 22 kHz SPEECH model only, with no real-time figures for the 44 kHz singing model. Mac: official MPS support (2025-03), but depends on unpinned PyTorch nightly and the repo is unmaintained. efegen/rvc-pipeline: does not exist (404); license and 6 GB VRAM claim unverifiable.
results.code_license: GPL-3.0 (Plachtaa/seed-vc LICENSE). The V2 tokenizer ASTRAL-quantization is also GPL-3.0. Both repos are archived. efegen/rvc-pipeline: no such repo.
results.weights_license: Plachta/Seed-VC HF repo: license gpl-3.0, ungated. Third-party weights fetched at runtime: lj1995 rmvpe.pt (MIT tag plus a 'research use only' rider in its license text), funasr/campplus Apache-2.0, nvidia/bigvgan_v2 MIT, openai/whisper-small Apache-2.0, FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice-300M hift.pt Apache-2.0. The README does not disclose the training-data provenance of the DiT weights.
results.output_rights: GPL-3.0 governs distribution of code and weights, not generated audio, and the README states no output-use restriction. Zero-shot cloning from a 1-25 s reference means consent controls must live in AURA itself, because Seed-VC has none.
results.hardware_notes: Official Apple Silicon support (requirements-mac.txt; mps device selection in the inference and GUI scripts), but on an unpinned torch nightly; untested here. The real-time GUI is benchmarked by the vendor only on an NVIDIA RTX 3060 Laptop (430 ms total, tiny speech model). No VRAM figure is published anywhere in the README. The '6GB VRAM' claim belongs to the non-existent efegen repo.

new_discoveries: Official RVC release 2.3.260718 (published 2026-07-21; changelog dated 2026-07-18/23) drops macOS. It targets Python 3.12 on Ubuntu 24.04 or Windows, has no MPS branch in configs/config.py, and removes run.sh. Its CPU requirements pin torch==2.4.1+cpu, which has no macOS arm64 wheel. The same release replaces the UVR5 separation backend with PyMSS (MIT; BS-RoFormer/MelBand-RoFormer, with MPS/MLX paths), adds FCPE pitch extraction, CUDA-graph real-time acceleration (vendor-claimed up to 4.7x on an RTX 4090D) and a Win64-only VST2/VST3 real-time plugin. The base model is unchanged, and RVCv3 is still only 'please look forward to it'. Impact: on Jon's M5 Pro, the official RVC WebUI is not a supported route.

Mac route for RVC is the community fork IAHispano/Applio: MIT plus a Terms of Use, v3.6.5 released 2026-09-19, active as of 2026-10-09. It has a macOS run-install.sh (Homebrew, PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK) and an MPS branch in rvc/train/train.py and rvc/infer/pipeline.py. Its HF repo IAHispano/Applio is tagged MIT with base_model lj1995/VoiceConversionWebUI, so it inherits the research-only rider question. Its ToU allows commercial use only when the user has rights and permissions for the audio.

The HF license file for RVC weights (lj1995/VoiceConversionWebUI, '使用需遵守的协议-LICENSE.txt') prepends a Chinese 'research use only' sentence (本软件仅供研究使用) to the MIT text, while the HF card metadata says plain MIT. Treat the RVC pretrained base models and rmvpe.pt as contested for commercial or open-source redistribution. Seed-VC and Applio both download this same rmvpe.pt.

RMVPE pretrained weights: yxlllc/RMVPE has no license file, and its README says training used MIR-1K + PTDB + M4Singer vocoder-synthesised data. M4Singer is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (NonCommercial). This is a provenance risk for any commercial or open-sourced AURA that bundles rmvpe.pt; FCPE (CNChTu/FCPE, MIT) is a candidate replacement pitch extractor, but its weights' provenance was not verified here.

Seed-VC and its V2 tokenizer ASTRAL-quantization were both archived on 2025-11-21. The author's active repo is Plachtaa/StreamVoiceAnon (ICASSP 2026; code Apache-2.0; HF weights tagged MIT but declare base_model fishaudio/fish-speech-1.5, which is CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0). It is a streaming SPEECH anonymization/VC model, not singing, and its README says 'Full MacOS support is still under construction'. It is not a drop-in Seed-VC singing successor.

Kimi's 'efegen/rvc-pipeline' reference pipeline does not exist publicly (GitHub 404, no HF or PyPI presence). Do not plan around it. Any claims sourced only from it (such as '6GB VRAM') should be dropped.

so-vits-svc (svc-develop-team) has been archived since 2023 and is AGPL-3.0. Avoid it as a dependency for an open-source or proprietary AURA. openvpi/DiffSinger (Apache-2.0, pushed 2026-10-08) is an actively maintained singing-synthesis alternative, though not verified in depth here.
